summary: ```# Marvelous Designer Quick Start (2025 Update) p11: Fabric Physical Properties and Unreal Engine Import ## Introduction to Fabric Properties In Marvelous Designer, you can express various fabrics through textiles and physical attributes. First, click on a fabric and drag it to the physical attribute bar at the bottom of the attribute editor. Marvelous Designer offers a rich array of fabrics for your reference and use. ## Fabric Preview and Adjustments The new version of Marvelous Designer has removed the fabric preview feature. However, you can still check the preview effect of the fabric by dragging it to the bar at the top window. The fabric preview allows you to quickly assess the general feel of the fabric. You can use these fabrics directly or utilize the preview fabrics to create the fabric you want. ### Physical Attribute Details Open the details bar at the bottom of the preview bar. The physical attribute details of the fabric are indicated by the gold line, the tail line, and the left and right smallest lines. Each of the four lines is controlled by the same attribute, allowing you to drag and move the slider to adjust the value of each direction separately. When you create a new version, the gold line defaults to the value direction, while the tail line is the 90-degree angle direction of the gold line. The tail line defaults to the 45-degree angle direction. You can check the gold line direction at any time through the 2D window and the 3D window or adjust the gold line direction to maintain its vertical position. ## Detailed Fabric Adjustments Let's delve into the fabric details to make more precise adjustments. First, examine the gold tail sand strength and the tail line strength. This group is controlled by the stretch performance of the fabric in these specific directions. Generally speaking, the physical attribute value on the toe line is lower than the value of the gold tail sand. The higher these values, the weaker the fabric's elasticity becomes, making it less likely to stretch due to gravity or pulling. Higher values produce fine, sharp wrinkles, resulting in a wrinkly and hard appearance. Conversely, lower values indicate better fabric elasticity, making it easier to create wrinkles. ### Texture Principles and Pattern Direction Let's add a texture principle for the shape pattern to directly explain the functions of the gold tail direction and the line direction. The pattern direction on the top panel is parallel to the gold line direction, representing it accordingly. When the simulation is not started, the gold line position on the panel is perpendicular to the ground in the 3D window. Press the control button to simulate, and you will notice that the gold line direction remains perpendicular to the ground in the middle of this piece of fabric. As you move to the left and right sides, the gold line direction gradually becomes oblique, aligning almost parallel to the ground. ### Strength Adjustments Due to the uniform radius of the top panel, the strength of the gold edge sand is the same as the strength of the angle line, keeping the bottom completely flat. If we increase the strength of the gold edge sand, the length in the middle will appear shorter and tighter. This is because the fabric becomes more elastic in the direction of the gold sand, making it less affected by gravity. The left side exhibits greater elasticity in the left and right directions, as the strength of the main resistance to gravity remains unchanged. ## Controlling Folds and Curvature Let's control the fold on the top panel. The button strength of the top panel, which moves up and down, drives the top panel in a vertical direction. You'll notice that the folds at the bottom of the top panel become more defined as the fabric tightens along the horizontal axis. If we want the folds on the left side of the shirt to be more pronounced, we should increase the value in the direction of the left diagonal line. You will see the folds become more apparent. ### Curve Intensity Group Next, we explore the curve intensity group. The higher the curve intensity, the better the support force of the fabric, making it easier to loosen during simulation, resulting in fewer, wider, and rounder folds. Conversely, lower curve intensity results in poorer support, leading to more, narrower, and flatter folds. When we apply this to the shirt, higher curve intensity enhances the support force of the fabric, making the folds less prominent and more broadly rounded. In contrast, lower curve intensity results in more pronounced, narrower, and flatter folds, causing the fabric to collapse more easily during simulation. ## Deformation Rate and Strength The deformation rate is related to the bending strength within the frame range, controlling the degree to which the fabric deforms. Like a small mountain peak, the top is the strongest area for folding and deformation. The tension of the deformation rate is maintained by an invisible cover that extends and controls the bending range. Typically, we adjust the deformation rate to 60, which is about half of the range. A deformation rate of 100 is a special value that controls the bending strength of the fabric. When set to 100, the folds of the sewing line will completely flatten. ### Adjusting Deformation Strength The tension of the deformation strength operates within the deformation rate range. The bending strength of the fabric is multiplied by the deformation strength, affecting the overall shape. When the deformation strength is set to 100, the fabric maintains the same shape as others. Reducing the deformation strength weakens the fabric's support, leading to a more pronounced fold. For example, setting the deformation strength to 20 means that the real bending strength is only 20% of what was initially set. When we simulate it, you will see that the fabric at the peak of the fold noticeably drops. Typically, we use fixed values for deformation strength, adjusting it to either 20 or 80 to control the existing folds, making them firmer or rounder. ## Weight Function and Fabric Density The weight function, previously known as density, controls the weight of the fabric. A heavier weight makes the fabric easier to stretch under gravity, reducing its tendency to float around and improving its feel. When creating clothing that looks good, we often want to avoid losing support due to weight, which can cause it to flatten. To counteract this, we can use the pressure function alongside the weight function to provide additional support from both inside and outside. ## Integration with Unreal Engine The interaction between Marvelous Designer and Unreal Engine has improved significantly. When exporting the USD file, selecting the clothing simulation information option enables the use of the super scroll function in Unreal Engine, allowing for the acceptance and editing of many fabric parameters from Marvelous Designer. Thank you for watching. See you in the next video! ```
